findings.finding: Toolchain is clean: build, vet, tests (including -race) all pass; gofmt reports no files; go.sum is empty (zero external dependencies); go.mod declares go 1.26.5 matching the local toolchain.
findings.evidence: `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` -> ok cmd/tdd-guard, ok controlplane, ok guard; `go test -race ./...` -> all ok; `gofmt -l .` -> empty; `wc -l go.sum` -> 0
findings.position: Go code compiles, vets, formats, and tests cleanly; no race under -race; no third-party deps.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED design gap: the guard never ties the RED and GREEN commands together or constrains what they are. `seal` only requires the red argv to exit non-zero and `verify` only requires the green argv to exit 0 and postdate the seal. An agent can satisfy the whole seal->verify contract with `--red-command false` and `--green-command true` without ever running tests.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad: `tdd-guard seal --red-command false` -> exit 0; `tdd-guard verify --green-command true` -> exit 0; status shows green recorded. actions.go:42 checks only ExitCode == 0 for red; actions.go:98-103 checks only ExitCode != 0 and isAfter(StartedAt, SealedAt) for green. No ArgvDigest comparison between seal.Red and green exists.
findings.position: The mechanical gate proves 'some command failed, then some command passed', not 'the sealed tests went red then green'. Severity depends on whether the argv is trusted to come from the skill/prompt rather than the agent.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED consequence of the 10MB cap: digestFileStreaming silently truncates via io.LimitReader, so two untracked files sharing their first 10MiB produce the same digest. diff-review staleness therefore cannot see edits past byte 10,485,760 of an untracked file. hardening_test.go:42-47 asserts this truncation as intended. Tracked files are unaffected (git diff HEAD).
findings.evidence: repository.go:424-425 `const maxBytes = 10 * 1024 * 1024; reader := io.LimitReader(file, maxBytes)`; no size/EOF check after io.Copy.
findings.position: Bounded memory was achieved by truncation rather than hashing the full stream (also bounded-memory); including file size in the digest would close the blind spot.

findings.source: README.md:50 vs guard/guard.go:316, guard/repository.go:373, guard/actions.go:128, guard/repository.go:280
findings.finding: PARTIAL README parity on 'streaming SHA-256 ... to prevent unbounded memory consumption during diff digesting'. Streaming with the cap applies only to untracked files in workingDiff. Sealed test files are still read whole with os.ReadFile in three places, and `git diff HEAD` output is buffered entirely in memory by captureArgv.
findings.evidence: guard.go:316 os.ReadFile; repository.go:373 same in collectTests; actions.go:128 same in reseal; repository.go:280 captureArgv("git","diff","HEAD") into bytes.Buffer.
findings.position: Claim holds narrowly (untracked files); the broader 'unbounded memory' wording overstates coverage.

findings.finding: README claim 'cross-platform path normalization (backslash/forward-slash)' is implemented and tested (TestBackslashPathNormalization). Normalization is unconditional on Linux, so a POSIX filename containing a backslash is mis-resolved — an edge case that only widens what is treated as sealed.
findings.evidence: actions.go:422 strings.ReplaceAll(candidate, "\\", "/"); actions.go:509 same in pathComponents; hardening_test.go:50-70.
findings.position: Claim matches implementation.

findings.finding: README claim 'in-memory directory caching during arch-check' is implemented: repositoryFilesWalk runs once and matchGlobCached filters per assertion; TestArchCheckGlobCaching asserts exactly one walk. Caveat: an assertion with an empty PathGlob passes `.` to ast-grep, bypassing the cached walk and the skippedDirectories filter.
findings.evidence: actions.go:269 `paths := []string{"."}`; actions.go:271-278; hardening_test.go:104-106.
findings.position: Claim matches implementation; mixed scan semantics between globbed and unglobbed assertions is a minor inconsistency.

findings.finding: README describes seal -> verify -> diff-review; the binary additionally exposes reseal, arch-check, hook, and status. README does not mention that arch-check results never block the Stop gate (stopBlockers omits arch review) nor that coverage is advisory-only. README calls the binary tdd-guard while the package, usage text, and messages call it anvil-guard.
findings.evidence: run.go:13-21 usage lists 7 commands; actions.go:346-369 stopBlockers checks changedTests/green/diffReview only; actions.go:75-79 coverage 'never gates'; bootstrap-tools.sh:60 builds ./cmd/tdd-guard as bin/tdd-guard.
findings.position: README undersells the surface and uses the tdd-guard name while code self-identifies as anvil-guard; not a functional mismatch.

findings.finding: README claim that CI runs go mod tidy verification is implemented.
findings.evidence: ci.yml:16 `go mod tidy`; ci.yml:17 `git diff --exit-code -- go.mod go.sum`.
findings.position: Claim matches CI.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED dead code: filesMatchingGlob is unreachable after the caching refactor replaced it with repositoryFilesWalk + matchGlobCached. No callers, no tests.
findings.evidence: `go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode@latest -test ./...` -> `guard/repository.go:163:6: unreachable func: filesMatchingGlob`.
findings.position: Safe to delete.

findings.finding: Ten exported controlplane functions have no callers anywhere in the repository and no test coverage: CanonicalDigest, SealGoal, ValidateGoal, SealAssignment, ValidateAssignment, SealDispatch, ValidateDispatch, DecodeWorkflowResult, DecodeRoute, DecodeSelection. controlplane is consumed only by guard/ (CommandEvidence, GuardSnapshot, digest prefix).
findings.evidence: deadcode lists all ten as unreachable; `grep -rln controlplane` outside controlplane/ hits only guard/actions.go and guard/repository.go; `go test -cover` -> controlplane 66.5%.
findings.position: Not bugs, but inflates the surface README/ADRs describe as enforced; the strict fail-closed Decode* entry points are entirely untested.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED comment/behaviour mismatch: ValidIdentifier's doc says it 'deliberately excludes whitespace and path traversal syntax', but the allowed set includes '.' and '/', so `a/../../etc` passes. Identifiers are used for IDs, not paths; paths use validRelativeScope (authority.go:328-334) which does reject traversal.
findings.evidence: codec.go:170 `case strings.ContainsRune("-_.:/@", character)` with no `..` check; contrast authority.go:332-333 path.Clean-based check.
findings.position: Doc comment overstates the guarantee; tighten the rule or fix the comment.

findings.finding: SUSPECTED lost-update race in the session touch log: recordTouchedRepositories does read-merge-write with no file lock. Two PreToolUse hooks for the same session running concurrently can each read the old log and the later rename wins, dropping the other's repository. writeJSON is atomic per write so corruption is impossible, only loss.
findings.evidence: session.go:46 readJSON, :71 writeJSON with no flock/O_EXCL between; guard.go:226-248 writeJSON uses CreateTemp+Rename.
findings.position: Real but narrow; the repository-from-target lookup in preToolUse still blocks sealed-test edits regardless, so loss only weakens Stop/PostToolUse coverage of touched repos.

findings.finding: SUSPECTED TOCTOU in verify: changedTests is checked before the green command runs, and the green command is arbitrary argv. A green command that edits a sealed test, runs the suite, and restores the file would pass verify. Corollary of the untrusted-argv finding.
findings.evidence: actions.go:87-93 pre-check; actions.go:94 runArgv; no post-run digest comparison.
findings.position: Only meaningful if the green argv is agent-controlled; same root cause as the false/true finding.

findings.finding: Symlinked untracked files are followed by os.Open when digesting the working tree, so content outside the repository is read and hashed (capped at 10MB, digest only, no exfiltration). FIFOs are not listed by `git ls-files --others` so no hang. Traversal in guard paths is handled physically via resolveSymlinks with a 40-hop bound and is well tested.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad: `ln -s /etc/hostname repo/link.txt; tdd-guard status` -> exit 0; `mkfifo repo/pipe.fifo; timeout 5 tdd-guard status` -> exit 0. collectTests filters entry.Type().IsRegular() (repository.go:347) but workingDiff does not.
findings.position: No exploitable traversal or symlink bypass found; symlink-follow in workingDiff is a minor robustness note.

findings.finding: No command injection: every external invocation uses exec.Command with an argv slice; nothing routes through a shell. A repository-relative path beginning with '-' could be misparsed by ast-grep as a flag, which surfaces as a non-zero exit -> error (fail closed).
findings.evidence: repository.go:40 exec.Command(argv[0], argv[1:]...); :89 append([]string{astGrepBinary(), "run", "--pattern", pattern, "--json"}, paths...); :110-112 non-zero exit returns error.
findings.position: Clean.

findings.finding: Input bounds are in place: hook payload capped at 64MiB with fail-closed refusal when a seal exists; controlplane contracts capped at 1MiB with depth limit 64, duplicate-key, surrogate, and trailing-data rejection.
findings.evidence: hook.go:69 maxPayloadBytes = 64 << 20, :76-82; codec.go:28-31, :49-81; bypass_test.go:42-75.
findings.position: Bounded, except the os.ReadFile/captureArgv cases noted under readme-parity.

findings.finding: Coverage: cmd/tdd-guard 100%, guard 82.4%, controlplane 66.5%. Holes: no test that seal/verify relate red/green argv; no test for concurrent touch-log writes; controlplane Decode*/Seal* sequence edge cases untested; resolveSymlinks maxSymlinkHops (cyclic symlink) path untested.
findings.evidence: `go test -cover ./...`; grep '^func Test' inventory (60 guard, 3 cmd, 38 controlplane); deadcode listing.
findings.position: Good on the hook/path surface, thin on the contract-decoding surface and on cross-process behaviour.

findings.finding: Minor: unsealedSourceChanges parses `git status --porcelain` v1 by slicing line[3:] and stripping quotes, but does not un-escape C-quoted paths (core.quotePath), so non-ASCII filenames are reported with escape sequences. Advisory-only path.
findings.position: Cosmetic.

findings.finding: Test suite passes: 22 passed, 0 failed (gofmt, ruff, shellcheck present so no skips).
findings.evidence: bash scripts/hooks/tests/test_hooks.sh | tail -3 -> '22 passed, 0 failed'
findings.position: green

findings.finding: shellcheck at warning severity reports exactly one issue across all 8 scripts: SC2088 tilde-in-quotes in a cosmetic echo. Info-level output is only SC2015 x24 and one SC2016 in test_hooks.sh — intentional idioms. Hook scripts themselves are shellcheck-clean.
findings.evidence: shellcheck -S warning -s bash <8 scripts> -> only 'scripts/bootstrap-tools.sh line 96: SC2088'
findings.position: essentially clean; one cosmetic warning

findings.finding: CONFIRMED side effect: running the test suite mutates the user's ~/.local/bin. Test 4 invokes project-bootstrap.sh --with-hooks, which sets install=1 and runs `install -m755 build-format build-lint build-guard $HOME/.local/bin/`, overwriting the symlinks bootstrap-tools.sh created with regular-file copies. CI runs the same script, so on a runner this also writes into $HOME.
findings.evidence: stat ~/.local/bin/build-guard -> '2026-08-28 13:05:17 regular file' (test run time); ~/.local/bin/build-hooks -> symlink dated 01:29; project-bootstrap.sh:24 `--with-hooks) withhooks=1; install=1;;` and :63 `install -m755 ... "$BIN/"`
findings.position: tests are not hermetic; they clobber user-level installs

findings.finding: CONFIRMED README parity break: README says every ~/.local/bin/build-* hook is a symlink so edits take effect immediately. bootstrap-tools.sh honors that (ln -sfn), but project-bootstrap.sh --install COPIES the three hook scripts (install -m755), replacing the symlinks. After project-bootstrap --install, edits to scripts/hooks/* no longer take effect until re-run.
findings.evidence: bootstrap-tools.sh:75 `ln -sfn "$ROOT/scripts/hooks/$h" "$HOME/.local/bin/$h"`; project-bootstrap.sh:63 `install -m755 ...`; README.md:21
findings.position: README claim is false after project-bootstrap --install

findings.finding: CONFIRMED guard bypasses for the 'never push/commit/merge to main' policy (empirical probes). Allowed: bare `git push` (upstream may be main), `git push origin HEAD` while on main, `git push origin master`, `git checkout main && git merge feat`, `git switch main; git merge feat`, `git branch -f main HEAD`, `git update-ref refs/heads/main HEAD`, `gh pr merge 1 --merge`, `jj bookmark set main -r @ && jj git push`, `B=main; git push origin $B`, `git push origin $(git branch --show-current)`, quote-splitting `git push origin ma""in`, and an alias defined in an earlier turn. Correctly denied: `git -C`, `sh -c "..."`, `cd x && git push origin main`, `/usr/bin/git`, tabs, `refs/heads/main`, `jj git push -b main`.
findings.evidence: probe loop: `jq -nc --arg c "$1" '{tool_input:{command:$c}}' | build-guard | jq -r .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` -> empty (allow) for each listed command
findings.position: guard is an advisory speed bump, not a security boundary; its header (lines 6-7) says 'deliberately narrow' while README.md:58 says it 'blocks critical violations'

findings.finding: CONFIRMED false positives (benign commands denied): `git push origin main-fix` (any branch beginning 'main-'), `git commit -m "fix main"`, `git commit -am "refactor main.go"`, `git merge-base main HEAD`, `echo "git push origin main"`, `grep "git push origin main" README.md`. Root cause: `main([^[:alnum:]_]|$)` treats '-' and '.' as boundaries and the pattern scans the whole command string including quoted message text.
findings.evidence: probe output: 'deny | git push origin main-fix', 'deny | git commit -m "fix main"', 'deny | git merge-base main HEAD', 'deny | grep "git push origin main" README.md'
findings.position: regex over-matches commit messages and hyphenated branch names

findings.finding: CONFIRMED: /tmp cargo-target blocking works for the literal test cases but is trivially evaded. Allowed: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR="/tmp/x" cargo b` (quoted), `cargo build --target-dir "/tmp/x"`, `cargo build --target-dir /tmp` (no trailing slash), `--target-dir=$TMPDIR/x`, `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/x`, `/dev/shm/x`. Denied correctly: unquoted forms, `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/x;`, `env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/x`.
findings.evidence: build-guard:23 `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=[[:space:]]*/tmp`, :24 `\-\-target-dir[= ][[:space:]]*/tmp/`; probe output shows allow for quoted forms
findings.position: quoting or dropping the trailing slash bypasses the tmpfs rule

findings.finding: CONFIRMED fail-open: if jq is absent (or the payload is malformed/empty), cmd is empty and the guard exits 0 silently — every command is allowed. Same fail-open applies to build-lint:8-9 and build-format:10-11. README's 'Verified jq availability at bootstrap' refers only to bootstrap-tools.sh:47; nothing at hook runtime checks for it.
findings.evidence: PATH=<dir with only bash+grep> bash scripts/hooks/build-guard <<< '{"tool_input":{"command":"git push origin main"}}' -> rc=0, no output; `echo 'not json' | build-guard` -> rc=0
findings.position: missing jq silently disables all three hooks

findings.finding: Harness dispatch: only `agy` selects the Antigravity payload shape; `claude`, `codex`, or no arg use the Claude shape. Feeding an agy-invoked guard a Claude-shaped payload (or vice versa) yields no cmd and a silent allow. build-hooks accepts `codex` but agents/codex/builder.md wires no hooks, so the codex arg is dead in practice.
findings.evidence: build-guard:11,13; `... | build-guard agy` with Claude payload -> no output, rc=0; `grep -n -i hook agents/codex/builder.md` -> no matches
findings.position: parsing is correct per harness but fails open cross-harness

findings.finding: Hook wiring parity gap: Claude builder wires Stop and SubagentStop to build-hooks; the Antigravity hooks.json has only PreToolUse/PostToolUse. hooks.json also uses `~/.local/bin/...` tilde paths and regex-alternation matchers; whether Antigravity expands tilde and supports alternation is unverified.
findings.evidence: agents/claude/builder.md:24-30 (Stop/SubagentStop); agents/agy/builder/hooks.json:4-52 (no Stop key)
findings.position: AGY builder lacks the Stop-time TDD verify gate

findings.finding: CONFIRMED portability defect: `find ... -printf '%f\n'` is GNU-only; BSD/macOS find has no -printf, so SKILLS is empty and the script aborts with 'no skills found' on macOS unless GNU findutils is installed. `mapfile` also requires bash 4+, so macOS stock bash 3.2 fails too.
findings.evidence: install-harness.sh:38 `mapfile -t SKILLS < <(cd "$ROOT/skills" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -printf '%f\n' | sort)`; :39 exits 1 when empty
findings.position: installer will not run on stock macOS

findings.finding: Guard regexes are POSIX ERE with bracket classes only (no \b, \s, or -P), so they are portable across GNU and BSD grep -E; the test at test_hooks.sh:58 enforces absence of \b.
findings.evidence: grep -n '\\b\|grep -P\|sed -i' scripts/hooks/* -> no matches in hook scripts; README.md:62
findings.position: hook regexes are portable; README accurate here

findings.finding: CONFIRMED install-clobber pitfall: `ln -sfn SRC DST` where DST is an existing real directory (e.g. a user's own ~/.claude/skills/jj/) does NOT replace it; it creates a symlink INSIDE it (DST/jj -> SRC). Install reports success while the harness keeps loading the user's original directory. --uninstall then runs `rm -f DST`, which fails on a directory and is silently ignored (no set -e). For regular files (agents/claude/*.md at :50), ln -sfn silently overwrites any user-authored file of the same name.
findings.evidence: scratchpad repro: mkdir dst/jj; touch dst/jj/userfile; ln -sfn src/jj dst/jj -> dst/jj/jj symlink created; rm -f dst/jj -> 'Is a directory' rc=1; `echo mine > dst/builder.md; ln -sfn src dst/builder.md` -> replaced
findings.position: install silently misbehaves on pre-existing real dirs and overwrites same-named user files

findings.finding: Uninstall deletes by name without checking that the target is a symlink pointing into this repo: a user's own file or symlink at those names (e.g. their own research.md agent) would be removed. README.md:18 says '--uninstall reverses it' with no caveat.
findings.evidence: install-harness.sh:54 `rm -f ~/.claude/agents/"$a".md`; :44 `rm -f "$d/$s"`
findings.position: uninstall can delete user files sharing a name

findings.finding: README parity gap on reversibility: install-harness.sh --uninstall removes agents/skills/codex TOML links but not ~/.local/bin/build-*, ~/.local/bin/tdd-guard, bin/, or dist/codex; bootstrap-tools.sh has no --uninstall and only recognises `--install` as $1 (`--help` prints the presence report instead).
findings.evidence: grep -n 'local/bin' scripts/install-harness.sh -> no rm of build-*; bootstrap-tools.sh:13 `[[ ${1:-} == "--install" ]] && install=1`
findings.position: '--uninstall reverses it' is only partially true

findings.finding: All scripts use `set -uo pipefail` without -e: a failed ln/mkdir/python3 step is not fatal and 'done.' still prints. The embedded python3 heredoc (install-harness.sh:90) runs unconditionally with naive frontmatter parsing (split('---', 2) at :109), so a malformed agents/codex/*.md produces a traceback after other harnesses were already modified. project-bootstrap.sh:37 runs install commands via `eval "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1`, which hides a sudo password prompt and can hang despite the 'non-interactively' claim.
findings.evidence: install-harness.sh:22,90,109-114,141-143; project-bootstrap.sh:3,29,37
findings.position: partial-failure states are possible and unreported

findings.finding: The .git/info/exclude local-ignore of .claude/settings.local.json only fires when .git is a directory. In git worktrees and jj workspaces (the builder's documented mode) .git is a file, so the settings file is not excluded and can leak into a commit — contradicting README.md:64.
findings.evidence: project-bootstrap.sh:103 `if [[ -d .git ]]; then`
findings.position: exclude is skipped for worktrees/workspaces

findings.finding: Minor robustness: build-format hardcodes `rustfmt --edition 2021` (edition-2024 crates may be misformatted); `prettier --log-level` is Prettier 3 syntax; build-lint checks for eslint config in the hook's cwd, not the edited file's project, so monorepo subpackages are skipped. Filenames with spaces are handled correctly.
findings.evidence: build-format:16 `rustfmt --edition 2021 "$f"`; :18 `prettier --write --log-level warn`; build-lint:15 `ls .eslintrc* eslint.config.* >/dev/null`
findings.position: minor robustness issues, advisory hooks only

findings.finding: build-hooks hardcodes $HOME/.local/bin/tdd-guard rather than PATH lookup; when absent it exits 127. For a Claude PreToolUse hook a non-2 non-zero exit is non-blocking, so a missing tdd-guard silently disables the TDD gate.
findings.evidence: HOME=/nonexistent scripts/hooks/build-hooks claude PreToolUse -> 'No such file or directory', rc=127
findings.position: TDD gate fails open when tdd-guard is not installed

findings.finding: Test coverage of the guard is limited to 5 literal happy-path strings; none of the bypasses or false positives above are covered, and test :39 ('format no-ops on missing file') is vacuous because build-format always exits 0. Several portability tests are grep-the-source assertions rather than behavioural tests.
findings.position: green but shallow

findings.finding: All six skill test suites pass: planner 19, build 10, code-review 21, docs 10, research 7, review-fix-loop 12 (79 total, 0 failures).
findings.evidence: `for d in planner build code-review docs research review-fix-loop; do python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/$d/tests -p 'test_*.py'; done` -> each prints OK.
findings.position: Suites are green; gaps below are about what they do not exercise.

findings.finding: ruff reports 44 issues, none of them bugs: 16 I001 import-sort, 8 EXE001, 8 PLW1510 subprocess.run without check=, 2 F401 unused importlib.util in tests, 1 F841 unused `sidecar` (skills/build/tests/test_build.py:84), plus FURB192/ISC004/RUF010/UP012/RUF007. CI does not run ruff on skills/.
findings.evidence: `ruff check skills/ --output-format concise` -> 'Found 44 errors, 22 fixable'; `grep -i ruff .github/workflows/*.yml` returns nothing.
findings.position: Style-only debt; no ruff gate exists in CI for skill scripts.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED idempotency bug: validate_plan() checks regexes against the stripped value but leaves the raw value in the plan, so a planId or issue key with leading/trailing whitespace passes validation yet produces a marker like `<!-- workcell-planner planId= planner-v3-sample issue=render-folio  -->` that ISSUE_MARKER_RE never matches. Every reconcile run then re-creates all issues.
findings.evidence: Probe: sample.sidecar.json with planId=' planner-v3-sample' and key 'render-folio '; render_plan and reconcile both exit 0; second reconcile against a snapshot built from the first run's payloads produced actions ['create_issue', 'create_issue'] instead of [].
findings.position: Whitespace-padded ids are accepted by validation but break marker round-tripping; reject or normalise (use the stripped value) in validate_plan.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED template-token injection (low severity): render() does sequential str.replace of `{{TOKEN}}` per key. A user-controlled string containing a later token name (e.g. summary = '{{MERMAID_JS}}') is not neutralised by html.escape (braces are not escaped), so the later replacement substitutes into it. For the planner the entire 3 MB mermaid bundle was injected as visible text into the lede. Not an XSS, but sidecar text can pull other sections' markup into arbitrary places.
findings.evidence: Probe with summary 'Injected {{MERMAID_JS}} token and <script>alert(1)</script>' -> rendered lede reads `Injected "use strict";var __esbuild_esm_mermaid_nm;...`. The <script> portion was correctly escaped.
findings.position: Escaping is correct; placeholder substitution order is the weakness. A single-pass regex substitution would close it.

findings.finding: HTML escaping is otherwise consistent: every interpolated user value goes through html.escape(quote=True), including attribute contexts. Class-name interpolations use only validated enum values. Mermaid source is escaped inside <pre class="mermaid">, the inlined bundle has `</script` neutralised (render_plan.py:443), and Mermaid runs with securityLevel strict (plan.html.tmpl:185).
findings.evidence: Manual read of all f-string HTML builders; `<script>alert(1)</script>` in summary rendered as `<script>`.
findings.position: No unescaped sink found beyond the token-substitution issue.

findings.finding: SUSPICION: mermaid_label() only neutralises double quotes, newlines and square brackets. `#...;` (Mermaid entity syntax), HTML tags and backticks pass through into quoted node labels; a title like 'Fix #123; …' may mis-render (fallback source panel is shown on failure).
findings.evidence: `mermaid_label('Fix #123; use `x` and bold "q"')` -> `Fix #123; use `x` and bold 'q'`.
findings.position: Diagram-level robustness gap, not a security issue given strict securityLevel; untested.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED false negative in ownership-overlap detection: globs_overlap relies on PurePath.match, which on Python 3.13 does not treat `**` recursively and is right-anchored, so a recursive glob vs a deeper concrete path is reported as non-overlapping. Two parallel issues owning `src/**` and `src/a/b/c.py` would pass validation and be built in the same wave.
findings.evidence: Probe (Python 3.13.5): globs_overlap('src/**','src/a/b/c.py') -> False; globs_overlap('src/a/b/c.py','src/**') -> False. Positive cases work: ('skills/planner/**','skills/**') -> True. Tests test_wave_ownership_overlap_* (test_build.py:160-165) do not cover the deep-path case.
findings.position: Overlap check is heuristic and misses recursive-glob vs deep path; PurePath.full_match (3.13+) or fnmatch-based expansion would be more reliable.

findings.finding: SUSPICION: validate_ownership_overlap treats wave 0 ('Ungrouped' per render_plan.py:327) like any other wave, so two ungrouped issues with overlapping hints hard-fail the build. It also prints a Warning to stderr and then raises with the same message. Free-text hints that are identical (e.g. 'backend service') also count as overlap.
findings.evidence: globs_overlap('backend service','backend service') -> True; wave grouping at lines 151-153 has no `wave > 0` filter.
findings.position: Defensible but inconsistent with the planner's 'wave 0 = ungrouped' semantics.

findings.finding: Re-running planner reconcile reopens any marked issue that a builder has closed as done (issue_differs treats state != 'open' as drift and the payload sets state:'open'). Documented as intended, but reconciling a plan after work has started reverts completed issues to open.
findings.evidence: Probe: snapshot with issue #1 closed, sidecar unchanged -> actions [('update_issue', 1, 'open')]. SKILL.md:111.
findings.position: Documented design, but hazardous mid-build; no guard (e.g. skip issues labelled status:done or closed via a merged PR).

findings.finding: Milestone adoption by exact title: when no milestone carries the plan marker, the reconciler adopts any milestone whose title equals planName and overwrites its description with the marker, dropping any human-written description.
findings.evidence: Probe: milestone #7 title 'Planner v3 Sample', description 'Human-written milestone description' -> update_milestone with description replaced by the marker.
findings.position: Intended adoption path; side effect is loss of pre-existing milestone description.

findings.finding: No gh command injection: subprocess.run uses an argv list (no shell), repo is regex-validated before interpolation into the REST path, issue/milestone numbers come from the API or int-typed args, bodies are passed via `--input -` on stdin as JSON. Timeouts enforced (30 s).
